== Life ==

Born in {{ill|Shinano Province|en|Shinano Province|qid=Q289250|lt=Shinano Province}}, Suwa District, Enchū was the son of Suwa Moritada. According to the {{ill|Kami Clan Genealogy|ja|神氏系図}}, he was a branch member of the {{ill|Suwa-taisha|en|Suwa-taisha|qid=Q218813|lt=Suwa-taisha}} Upper Shrine family and inherited the position of {{ill|Jitō|en|Jitō|qid=Q1329805|lt=jitō}} for {{ill|Shinomiya-shō|ja|四宮荘|qid=Q136731801}} Funayama village in {{ill|Hanishina District, Nagano|en|Hanishina District, Nagano|qid=Q726661|lt=Hanishina District}}, leading to his alternate name, '''Kosaka Enchū'''. His holdings also included lands in {{ill|Etchū Province|ja|Etchū Province}}, Takagi Village, and the villages of Miyake-gō Jūniri and Akanoi in {{ill|Ōmi Province|en|Ōmi Province|qid=Q843882|lt=Ōmi Province}}. The Suwa clan served as {{ill|hikan|ja|被官|zh|被官|qid=Q11626601}} under the {{ill|Hōjō clan|en|Hōjō clan|qid=Q834364|lt=Hōjō clan}}, and Enchū’s uncle Suwa Tokimitsu was also an official of the Kamakura shogunate, fostering Enchū’s upbringing and service in Kamakura.

After the fall of the Hōjō clan, Enchū traveled to Kyoto and, through the mediation of {{ill|Musō Soseki|en|Musō Soseki|qid=Q384703|lt=Musō Soseki}}, entered the service of {{ill|Ashikaga Takauji|en|Ashikaga Takauji|qid=Q297107|lt=Ashikaga Takauji}}. He rose through the Ranks from {{ill|Hyōjōshū|ja|評定衆|2=es|3=Hyōjōshū|4=ja|5=評定衆|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Hyōjōshū|13=User:Immanuelle/Hyōjōshū|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11288036}} to protectorate administrator, eventually overseeing the construction of {{ill|Tenryū-ji|ja|天竜寺}}. He later became the administrator of {{ill|Sōroku|ja|禅律方|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zen temple affairs|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 僧録|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10889387}}, managing Zen-related issues. Enchū also contributed to the revival of the Suwa clan, whose main line had declined after the {{ill|Nakasendai Rebellion|ja|中先代の乱|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Revolt of Nakasendai|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q10871756}}, and helped establish a system where warriors across Shinano participated in the annual Suwa Upper Shrine festival.

In {{ill|Enbun|en|Enbun|qid=Q1145071|lt=Enbun}} 1 ({{ill|1356|en|1356|qid=Q6130|lt=1356}}), Enchū completed the {{ill|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|fa|سابقه مصور زیارتگاه سووا|id|Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba|ja|諏方大明神画詞|qid=Q11631818|lt=Suwa Daimyōjin Ekotoba}}, which bore a postscript by Takauji. This work spread Suwa faith throughout various strata of society, including the court nobility. As part of Takauji’s initiative to establish a national network of {{ill|Ankoku-ji|en|Ankoku-ji|qid=Q10158536|lt=Ankokuji temples}}, Enchū founded {{ill|Ankokoji (Chino City)|ja|安国寺 (茅野市)|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinano Ankokuji|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q20043040}} near the Suwa Upper Shrine with Musō Soseki as its founding abbot.

Enchū also inherited knowledge of {{ill|Falconry|ja|鷹匠|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/falconry|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 鷹狩|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q211011}} from the {{ill|Q11536451|ja|祢津氏|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nezu clan|ja_comment=jawiki redirects to 根津氏|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11536451}}, a branch of the Suwa clan, as recorded in the {{ill|Kami Clan Genealogy|ja|神氏系図}}. This expertise was passed down among the heads of the Kyoto Suwa clan, and in {{ill|Civilization|en|Civilization|qid=Q8432|lt=Bunmei}} 5 ({{ill|1473|en|1473|qid=Q6594|lt=1473}}), Suwa Tadakuni collaborated with the {{ill|Asukai family|en|Asukai family|qid=Q11665942|lt=Asukai clan}} on annotated falconry waka poetry for {{ill|Ashikaga Yoshimasa|en|Ashikaga Yoshimasa|qid=Q447034|lt=Ashikaga Yoshimasa}}, recorded in the {{ill|Taka Hyakushu-chū|ja|鷹百首註}}. Tadakuni’s son, Suwa Sadamichi, compiled a treatise on falconry titled {{ill|Taka Kikigaki Shōshō|ja|鷹聞書少々}}.

Enchū also excelled in waka and renga poetry, with works selected for the {{ill|Shinsenzai Wakashū|en|Shinsenzai Wakashū|qid=Q1143262|lt=Shin Chokusenshū}}, {{ill|Shingoshūi Wakashū|en|Shingoshūi Wakashū|qid=Q288358|lt=Shin Goshūishū}}, and {{ill|Tsukubashū|en|Tsukubashū|qid=Q3007417|lt=Tsukubashū}}.<ref>[https://www.ro-da.jp/shinshu-dcommons/museum_history/03OD0624101600] "Kami Clan Genealogy: Copy of Maeda Manuscript"</ref>
